scope: Read-only sealed source/adapters and fixed-wheel bytes; prospective single execution checkout recovery
path_reasoning: Both dependency locations are relative to the root argument. Reconstructing the same relative paths under a new real checkout root satisfies the unchanged byte reads and path identity checks.
Every sealed VTracer member (2) and Pathops member (5) is reproduced exactly by the corresponding fixed wheel; both wheel hashes and metadata versions match the sealed requirements.
The V24 kernel and V25-V28 adapters remain at their pinned raw SHA. Each adapter continues to compile the checked V24 source and compare exact original profiles/replayed SVG semantics.
The original validator derives REPO_ROOT from its own file. Running that file inside the new checkout targets the new root without editing the validator or sealed kernels.
required_execution_sequence: Freeze the old checkout as read-only history; stop every old business writer. Snapshot the current source/evidence/state hashes and real consumed tool calls before copying.
Create one new actual checkout within the allowed workspace. Preserve the same task identity, mainline, current revision/history and real tool-consumption ledger; Root is the only business writer.

Copy current source and the full reachable real evidence/private input closure as exact bytes. Do not rely on links/junctions to old private evidence: checked path resolution must remain inside the new root.

Do not copy the inaccessible old installed package directories, their ACLs, local bytecode caches or stale import state. Rebuild both exact original site-packages paths from the checked fixed wheels, verifying all members and the seven sealed SHA entries.

Start a fresh bundled Python process with -s -X utf8 -B, cwd at the new checkout. Run the original validator entrypoint directly. Do not use the old verified_restore preloading wrapper and do not mutate sys.modules to conceal a wrong module path.

Preflight actual VTracer and Pathops imports under their exact expected new paths, versions and raw member hashes. Then run the unchanged complete historical/native validator and require its genuine result.

Treat the new checkout as the sole execution location after handoff; retain the old checkout and its failures as frozen history. Do not run two independent state writers or invent a second authoritative task system.
alternative_reason: The sealed function reads the old expected files directly before import. Merely changing sys.path or restoring to a different directory cannot satisfy those reads. Replacing/renaming old installed package directories would modify the checkout designated frozen; patching the sealed loader, faking __file__, symlinking around path bounds or skipping history is outside the accepted constraints.
limits: This is a recovery-layout judgment, not proof that a new checkout has passed. Its readable copy/evidence closure and actual imports remain untested until Root performs the migration/preflight.
All remaining source/evidence/renderer/native-state assertions stay active. Any missing/unreadable private input or byte mismatch must remain a real blocker rather than being declared passed.
No aesthetic acceptance or new image/Figma artifact is inferred from dependency reconstruction.
The actual second imagegen consumption must survive the rollback and relocation; restoring old state bytes alone is not a budget reset.
